utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. O'Sullivan, I had expected Mr. Milutinovic to be absent this afternoon, but he's also absent this morning. And the informal information I have is that there seems to be some miscommunication about the arrangements for his absence. Do you have any difficulty with us proceeding in his absence this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And I understand you -- he has waived his right to be present this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, to receive treatment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, Mrs. Malaj.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The solemn declaration to tell the truth, which you took at the beginning of your evidence, continues to apply to your evidence today. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, no, no. There's no need to repeat -- there's no need to repeat that. I was just confirming with you. There is no need to repeat that. Sorry, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought I had to repeat it today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Good morning to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, yesterday when we winded up for the day you said that you are a housewife and that you know nothing about the KLA and that you have nothing to do with the KLA. My first question this morning is, can you confirm for me that your village, Korenica, is one of the villages in the Carragojs valley?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you recall -- actually, let me ask you something else first. In your village, was there ever any KLA activity?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to draw your attention to your first statement that you gave to the investigators of the OTP on the 31st of August and the 1st of September 2000. On page 2 of the B/C/S version, it's page 2 in the English version, paragraph 5, and page 2 of the Albanian version, also paragraph 5. You said, "We were terrified because the Serb forces started shooting at KLA positions in Nec, Smolice, Pacaj, Ramoc and the other villages of the Carragojs valley." Is it correct that that is what you stated?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Let's deal with it this way. How far away is Nec from Korenica?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is also a village of Duzhnje first. I would say about -- I haven't been in that direction, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the village of Nec is very close to Korenica, right?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Along the main road, it's not far. There is first of all this Duzhnje and then Nec is after Duzhnje.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. How far away is the village of Smolice from Korenica?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you at all. I've never been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: What about the village of Pacaj?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just know the names of the villages but I don't know how many kilometres away they are but they are around there somewhere. On the other side of Meja, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mrs. Malaj. Since you were never there and you could mention the names of these villages where the KLA was, you will agree with me that you heard about that from the members of your own household, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who were members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's not clear to me what that question relates to. Heard about what from members of her own household?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was some misinterpretation. I just asked the witness to agree with me that since she was a housewife, and since she never went to these villages, that this information about KLA staffs and headquarters and places where the KLA was she heard from the members of her own household who were also members of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there are about five different questions in there. First of all you'll need to establish what her knowledge of the KLA was. You have established nothing so far from her about knowledge of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Madam you said that you're a housewife. You said that you were never in these villages. How come you know about these activities of the KLA from these villages?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: She hasn't said a word about knowing about the activities of the KLA as yet. You have to establish first of all when she knows about the activities of the KLA. The only answer you've had so far on that subject was that there was no KLA activity in her village. And the fact that she knows of the existence much a village nearby establishes nothing about knowledge of the KLA activity there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: I'm going to read out again for you part of your statement, the one that I read out a few moments ago. "We were scared because the Serbian forces were engaged in shooting against the KLA positions." My first question is -- my first question is: What do you mean by that when you say "KLA positions"?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I mean is that they were taking advantage of the situation and shooting at us in our homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: So KLA positions were in your houses, right?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not in our houses but they were shooting, there was police in Korenica and in Duzhnje and from that side, they were shooting at us, at my home. Not only at my home but at everyone else's home and you can still see on the walls the holes from the bullets, but fortunately there --

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Excellent, Mrs. Malaj. Do I understand you correctly that forces started opening fire at positions of the KLA and that the KLA did not respond with gunfire?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. All I can tell you is that they were shooting at us, at my home and at other people's homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Malaj. That will do, as far as I'm concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, in your statement, as was pointed out you refer to Serb forces being engaged in shooting against KLA positions located in, and then a number of villages are named and you've been given the names. Now, how do you know anything about that activity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As to the KLA, I don't really have any information about them. That's what was said at the time in 1998. They said that we were -- that they were after the KLA but I was never there myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But from whom did you hear that there were said to be KLA positions located in Nec and Smolice and other villages nearby?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know Smolice, Nec, they are only names. I don't know anything more about them. When I was at home, I heard the words, people were talking about Nec and about Smolice, but I have never seen them myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Look, again, please at your statement, at the page you're being referred to which is page 2, and the fifth [Realtime transcript read in error "first"] paragraph. And the paragraph starts with the words, "during summer 1998." Do you have that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's the fifth paragraph, I see the translation or at least the interpretation says first. It's the fifth paragraph of page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: She has two statements, so she may be looking at the wrong one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you now have that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I found it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If you look at the last sentence in it, the middle -- beginning in the middle line roughly, "We were scared because the Serbian forces were engaged in shooting against KLA positions located in Nec and Smolice and other villages of the Carragojs valley." Now you're saying there that the Serbs were shooting against KLA positions. Now, from whom did you learn that there were KLA positions in these villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As to the positions, we had heard about them, they existed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you know, can you remember from whom you heard that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. Someone -- someone said that, must have said that. A lot of people said that at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, I will try to avail myself of this opportunity as you have your first statement before you now, and I would like to draw your attention to this paragraph of that same statement, where you say, "Starting from the 7th of or 8th of March 1999, the men from our village would regularly go to the mountain at night-time because the situation was extremely tense." Can you tell us why it was that men from your village regularly went to the mountains at night-time?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: They went away because they were afraid of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: And during the night there was no army, it didn't exist, is that what you're trying to tell me?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: We heard from other places that massacres occurred but they were always in the morning, so they went at night until the time was over, just the way it happened on the 27th of April, in the morning. It was in the morning, the massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say to me that they would leave their families behind and that they would hide in the mountains? Is that correct? They would leave their families to be exposed to what you described just now? Is that what you're trying to say?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not because of the danger. Dragan Micunovic, they -- if he said go away, get -- go away. It was his order. He was the one who said it. He proposed that the men of the village leave because nothing would have happened to the women.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Malaj. Excellent, Mrs. Malaj. Now I'm going to draw your attention to the next paragraph. Here you said, "From the 7th or the 8th of March, men started going." Next paragraph. "At the end of March, Dragan Micunovic said to Gjon Prelaj to bring his orders to the villagers that men had to go." So according to your own statement the men started going into the mountains on the 7th and 8th of March and what you are saying now is contained in your statement. It was at the end of March, you say in your statement. How can you explain that to me?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question, please? I didn't really understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, you said to me that the men started going into the mountains when Dragan Micunovic ordered them to do so. In your own statement, it is stated completely differently. In the paragraph I mentioned to you, you said that from the 7th or 8th of March the men regularly went into the mountain and in next paragraph, right in the next paragraph, you said that it was only at the end of March 1999 that Dragan Micunovic sent a message that the men should go into the mountains.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. That's a bit misleading. The statement said the men regularly went to the mountain at night time. The order does not necessarily reflect that it wasn't regarding the daytime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't understand. Perhaps there is a misinterpretation. I cannot really follow the transcript and -- well, my question was the following. Could the witness explain to me the difference between what she is saying today and what she stated in her statement, the one that I refer to. I read it out. I don't know if it's necessary for me to repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: In the statement you said on the 7th or 8th of March, the men or rather from the 7th or 8th of March, the men from our village would regularly go to the mountains at night-time and in the next paragraph you say that at the end of March, 1999, Dragan Micunovic ordered that the men had to go and hide in the mountains. So according to your first statement, the men went into the mountains before allegedly Dragan Micunovic issued this order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you answer the question, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. In my statement here, I remember it was the end of March, 1999, Dragan Micunovic gave us an order to leave the village at night, every night, until the 4th of April. It was the Easter Monday. Until that time, the men of the village were in the mountains every night at the order of Dragan. And then he gave another order for the men to return, "po." But at the same day, the day he gave the order for the men to leave, they came back. And then he gave another order for the men to go to the mountains and for the women to wait by the trucks to be sent away to different locations. That's what I wrote in my statement here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, today a few moments ago in response to your question why you said in your statement that from the 7th and 8th of March the men went into the mountains at nights time, you said that it was ordered by Dragan. Do you see that there is a difference? According to your statement the men set out at the beginning of March, and Dragan drew their attention to this only at the end of March. Can you explain this discrepancy to me?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the beginning and at the end, everything that took place in our village took place under the -- under his orders. It was at the beginning and the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Are you now trying to tell me that even before the 7th of March, there was yet another order issued by Dragan Micunovic that you never mentioned before, that this is the first time you're mentioning that order?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no reason before -- at the beginning to say that, but that's the way he acted. That's what he told us to do from the very start to the very end because at the beginning we had no problem with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. This is my question. When you had no problems whatsoever in the beginning, before March, that's what you said in your statement too, why was it that from the 7th or 8th of March onwards, the men went into the mountains at all?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He gave us the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mrs. Malaj. Do you know that in April 1999, in the area where the cemetery is of Korenica, an army patrol was attacked and Vuckovic, Dobrica, a soldier, and Lapadatovic, Miroslav, another soldier, were wounded? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that and that's not true. No soldier was ever killed at the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: You said not a single soldier was ever killed at the cemetery. Was a soldier ever killed anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our village, no. No one. I can't tell you anything about other villages, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know a person called Hatemi Kameri?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean a woman, it would be Hateme Kameri, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Do you know her?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes. She was a neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Is she from your village? I beg your pardon. The question came before I got the interpretation. Of course, if she is your neighbour then she is from your village. Do you know whether this neighbour of yours, in her statement to the OTP, stated that expulsions from Korenica -- or rather, that this action in Korenica was carried out by paramilitaries and the local police? Did you know that and, if so, what would be your comment as regards that since yesterday you said there were three categories, three different categories of people?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. She was a Muslim woman but I don't know what happened to her in her house because I wasn't there but I know about my house and I told you about it. I know that there were three groups, three categories of military who came into the courtyard of my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, do I need to remind you that yesterday you said that the same thing was happening in all of the houses in your village?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that doesn't necessarily mean it was being done by three different groups at each house in the village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think that's a matter for comment, Mr. Hannis. Carry on, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It's been entered into the transcript that this was a neighbour. I wanted to move on to another topic and I am to conclude soon, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, yesterday you stated, and you mentioned that in your statement as well, this being the second statement dated the 6th and the 9th of September, at page 3 in the B/C/S, in the English pages 3 and 4, the last paragraph on the third and the first paragraph on the fourth page, and in the Albanian version, it is page -- if I may have a moment, Your Honour -- yes, in the Albanian, that is also page 3. You state there, "We invited the local priest, who negotiated with the forces who were escorting us to allow us to go to two villages in the Gjakova municipality, those being Racan and Osekpashe, but they refused that and wouldn't allow us to go there. They only let us go towards Albania and they told us that unless we went there, we would be killed, executed." When you say "we" here, did you have in mind that column of refugees containing about 1.000 people?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the column of refugees, for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. Mrs. Malaj, did you know that a number of people from your column did not in the end go to Albania?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what happened to us but I can't tell you what happened to everyone else. I don't know. I don't know. I know approximately that -- well, we got -- that I think that most of them got there but I can't tell you about everyone. I can't tell you about individuals, where they ended up, but I know that the people in our village got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Do you know a person by the name of Merita Deda?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know her. I have known her since I was a child, when she was little, but I saw her, I met her here too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Do you know whether she went to Albania?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, she didn't. As far as I know, she didn't, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Did you know that as regards the same column and the same incident, she states in her statement that soldiers of the Yugoslav armed forces approached the priest and told him that those who were on tractors and carts will be allowed to go towards the border but those who were on foot should return to their villages, she arrived at Bistrazhin and stayed with her relatives. After that she returned to her house. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the events, we spent a long time in Bistrazhin. But policeman went to her, talked to her, another policeman talked to us, so some were forced to return to Bistrazhin and I guess she returned home.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Therefore, Mrs. Malaj, if I understood your answer correctly, you were forced to return to Bistrazhin, to your homes. This is what you stated.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, Merita as well, she was asked to go back and she was settled somewhere in Bistrazhin. But we went to Bistrazhin, to Xerxe and we've been going back and forth six times, and at the end they told us, don't come back to your homes, otherwise you will get killed but go straight to Albania. As far as what I've heard myself, that's -- that's different. We had been walking without food, without water, until we were exhausted.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But Mrs. Malaj, I read out a portion of the statement of that person whom you know. As regards that part of the route. And the departure to Albania, that person stated that together with the other people who were on foot, she was returned to the village by the Yugoslav armed forces, whereas those who had other means of transport, some sort of vehicles, were allowed to move on. They were not forced to turn back. They could continue towards Albania. Could you explain to me the discrepancy between your statement and that other statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. This has been asked and answered and I don't think this is a proper way to cross-examine this witness, with something another witness might have said, another witness who was one of a thousand people in a convoy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't think, Mr. Hannis, you can put your finger on anything here as improper and the issue is one of reliability. Mr. Bakrac is using a statement which is that of a witness we are going to hear from shortly. There ever been in the overall context, I think it appropriate to repel this objection and to allow the examination to continue on that basis. Carry on, Mr. Bakrac. You'll need to repeat the question, though.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, would you be so kind as to explain to me how is it possible that we have such great differences, such discrepancies between your statement and a statement of another person who was in the same column as you were? Would you allow for the possibility that you didn't tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object, lack of foundation. He's trying to argue there is a discrepancy. That assumes that she was told by the same person that Merita was told. She may have been talking to a completely different person. We need some more foundation before he can say there is a discrepancy between the two. They are not necessarily inconsistent with each other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This question is rather -- the word discrepancy was used in the previous question but used in a different way. And I think I accept Mr. Hannis's criticism of this question, Mr. Bakrac. And you'll need to formulate this in a way which doesn't presuppose a conclusion that may not be justified.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, would you agree with me if I said that you were not forced to go to Albania? That would be my first question, that you were not forced to go to Albania.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree with you here because we were forced and there was a great deal of force used. We were not given even five minutes' time to sit and our children were hungry, they didn't have to eat or drink. They used a great deal of force.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: But Mrs. Malaj, you've confirmed to me a minute ago that a person who was with you in the column remained in Kosovo, she returned to the village of Bistrazhin; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct, but that's how they were forced to go. That's where they were forced to go. The people behaved the way they were ordered to do by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, can you give us some indication of the distance that Bistrazhin is from your own village of Korenica? How long would it take you to walk from one to the other?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On foot? From the moment we left to Bistrazhin we walked for about four or five hours from the moment we left the park.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In kilometres, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. You were going to say something, Mr. O'Sullivan?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Just wanted to state for the record that during Mr. Bakrac's cross-examination, Mr. Milutinovic entered the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mrs. Malaj. My name is Branko Lukic and together with Mr. Dan Ivetic and Mr. Ogrizovic, I appear on behalf of General Lukic before this Tribunal. I would kindly ask you to bear with us so that we could try and clarify some things concerning your previous statements. I wanted to go back to where my learned friend Mr. Bakrac left off when he asked you about the departures of the males from the villages to the mountains. Can you tell us which mountains exactly they went to?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the mountains in Korenica, so they left the houses and went to the surrounding mountains, no where else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Which mountains are there in the surroundings of Korenica, Mrs. Malaj?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's our mountains. I don't know. We call them our mountains, the mountains of Korenica. That's our land there. They don't have any other name.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Isn't Korenica in a valley, Mrs. Malaj?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that but it's five kilometres away from Gjakova, the city of Gjakova.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand you. What is five kilometres away from Djakovica, Mrs. Malaj?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village of Korenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I fail to understand why we can't understand each other over such a simple question and why are we referring to Korenica? I asked you about the mountains and their names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: She answered that question, Your Honour. She also answered the question about whether Korenica was in a valley by saying she didn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't see anything wrong with pursuing that, I have to say, so carry on Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you don't know that the village you reside in is actually in a valley, Mrs. Malaj?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: The village is on a plain. I don't know what valley you're talking about. And there are -- our village is very good and flat area. There are mountains around. The mountain which I mentioned earlier, where men were hiding, they were our property. It's not a valley. It's not like that. It's more like a hill.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The mountains you are referring to, Mrs. Malaj, since you are trying to avoid giving the answer, I am going to tell you that, they border with Albania?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Hold on, hold on. Mr. Lukic, what basis have you for saying that the witness is trying to avoid giving the answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Because he's avoiding to give me how far those mountains are or where are located. I cannot extract this simple answer from this witness. We have just begun and I have a problem with her in geographic terms. We have to move on much more serious questions. We cannot finalise this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I consider that your accusation is unfounded and that you ought to withdraw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you can take it that if the Bench here consider that a witness is trying to avoid answering questions, it will take action on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And if you wish the Bench to take action because you think we are not, and that a witness is being evasive then you should address us on it separately and not make accusations towards the witness. There are ways of dealing with these matters and it is not appropriate for you to make these comments about the witness's approach to the answering of questions directly to her in examination of her. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Malaj, the mountains you are referring to, are they about five kilometres away from your house?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's -- 100 metres away is the hill/mountain where our men were hiding. It's not near the border. It's just above my house, a hundred metres further away. It's where our men were hiding.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That's all I wanted you to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, how long would it take a person to get from your house to where you say the men were hiding?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ten, 15 minutes. It's very close to our house, and that is part of the land that we possess, and in the area which is part of our land, that's where the men were hiding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you about your statement dated the 31st of August, 2000. Although my learned friend Mr. Bakrac touched upon the topic nevertheless I need to go back to that and that is the extent to which you were familiar with the existence of the KLA in the area of your village.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was not a single one in our village, but as far as I'm aware, they were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we please put a map in front of the witness, the map of the Djakovica municipality, being P35? Could we please have the image -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could it be enlarged a bit on my screen, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Can you enlarge it in the area, eastern of Djakovica? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Should it not be west?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, west. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Malaj, I hope you will forgive me for my pronunciation, Lugu i Carragojes, up to the river Keqe, what area is that if I refer to those two names?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Reka e Keqe, as we call it, this is a border area. This is bordering Albania. But I come from the village of Korenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know Lugu i Carragojes? Do you know where that is?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've only heard the name but I've never been to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us where this area is?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me to point on the map or in general?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] If you can try because it's not possible to be pointed on this map. Oh, yes, now, if you can point on this map, please?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the villages or what do you want me to point to?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If you can show us the stretch that goes from Lugu e Carragojes to Reka e Keqe. [Interpretation] Would you please put a circle around this area, please?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. This is Korenica, Popoc, here. And I've encircled all the villages there, Korenica --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Shishman, Popoc, Smolice, Ponoshec, Morin, Brovin, Mulic, Butush, Kushar [phoen], these are the other villages. Nec. Ramoc is further away. Shishman, here. Butush. Not this one here. Guske. As far as I know, these are the ones, but I don't know any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mrs. Malaj. That will do. Now I'm going to ask you the following. Do you know who Malaj Fila is? She was also born in Guske and she also married in Korenica, like you.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj Fila, in her statement that she gave on the 20th of October 2001, this is a statement she gave to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal, she says the following. I'm going to read the English version because I have it right in front of me so I don't want to make any translation mistakes. "[In English] As far as I know UCK, KLA, held front lines in Ramoc, Nec, Junik, and in other villages from Lugu i Carragojes to Reka e Keqe." [Interpretation] Will you agree with me that this Prosecution witness is asserting that KLA positions were on these positions that you marked for us just now on this map?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you are saying, about Fila Malaj, like myself, she has heard about things. She is a housewife too, and she heard about it. She heard about the people in the village but she has never seen it. I think so. However, she -- she has seen her own husband and son being burned inside their house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Even more reason for her not to lie about the existence of the KLA, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's argumentative and unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You see, again I agree because the statement that witness gave starts with the words, "As far as I know," which is far from an assertion, albeit Mr. Lukic described it as an assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you, Your Honour, may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, you may, but you know, the last comment was indeed a comment rather than a question. Let's confine this examination to questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'll do my best, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Malaj, this morning we found a document. We have not put it into the system and we don't know what it's about at all because it's in the Albanian language. With the permission of the Court, I would like to have this placed on the ELMO so that Mrs. Malaj can tell us what this is about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We do not consider it appropriate to do that, Mr. Lukic, to use the witness as a translator of a document that you say you know nothing about. So move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then without showing the document I'll try to ask her whether she knows who Xheladin Malaj is.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no Xheladin Malaj in our village. Xheladin, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is there a person by the name of Spend Malaj in your village?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. What about him?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was in the sector of the military police in the 131st Brigade of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I've never heard such a thing about that person, that he worked in what you're saying he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Gani Malay and Islam Malaj, are these persons who lived in your village?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, these are not part of our family. There are many people with the surname of Malaj, but in Korenica, they are not part of our family, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The question was whether they lived in your village, not whether they were members of your family. Can you answer that? Did they live in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, never. They are not from our village, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will compare the list of inhabitants of your village to these names and in connection with that, I'm asking you whether Dem Malaj born on the 6th of June 1981 is from your village, a member of the special unit of the Black Eagles in the KLA?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There is no one in our family with that name, no. There is no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know the name of Ardian Malaj?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ardian Malaj, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that he was within the 131st Brigade of Ratish [phoen] and that he belonged to the mortar unit within it? The KLA, of course.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This Ardian Malaj has lived in Switzerland since he was five years old. Now he's married to a Swiss woman. He wasn't in Kosovo at the time or in Korenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is there a person named Valdet Malaj in your village, also a member of the Black Eagles unit of the 131st Brigade of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not someone from our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What about a person, again I'm apologising for my pronunciation, Siptara Malaj, is that person from your village too?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. There is lots of people with the surname Malaj, all over the place. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I asked you whether this person is from your village, Mrs. Malaj.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if you can describe the person to me. I don't know. They are all called Malaj. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Of course, I'm going to tell you very gladly. On the 5th of February 1999 he gave a statement to the OTP, he's a member of the KLA, and he says, well, let me not recount the statement now but he speaks of his participation in many clashes and in a lot of the fighting that the KLA had with the Serb forces. At the end he belonged to the 134th Brigade of the KLA, commanded by Tahir Zema?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our family, I can tell you that none of the women in the village, in our village, is related to what you're saying. All the women of the family Malaj are housewives and they are all tending to their households, not doing what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Madam, I don't know whether we understand each other right. The name of this person, the way I pronounce it, is Siptar, Malaj, it's a man?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That is not the name that was originally given. It was given as Siptara Malaj and that may explain the misunderstanding but can I also ask you, is this -- the date you say the statement was taken accurate, the 5th of February, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, Your Honour, that's what it says on the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, shall we just conclude on this particular person who is a man? I apologise at the very outset for perhaps my poor pronunciation.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you that this person is not a member of our family. There is no Siptar Malaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll just take you back to something that Mr. Bakrac asked you about as well but I'm not going to put the same question to you as he did. It has to do with a paragraph that is in paragraph 7 on the second page of the B/C/S version, English version, second page, last paragraph, and in the Albanian version page 3, paragraph 2. When you talked about Dragan Micunovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Which of the two statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first statement. [Interpretation] The first statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're talking about Dragan Micunovic, who, as you said, ordered the men to go into the mountains and that the women should stay behind. What was your feeling about this order of his that the men should go into the mountains? Did you take it as assistance or as a threat? It is not clear what you mean by this when you say that he ordered someone to hide.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what his purpose was. I don't know whether it was assistance or what. I really don't know. All the men obeyed him. What he said, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He said that the women should remain in the villages and wait for buses and trucks that would take you in an unknown direction. Did that actually happen? Did these buses and trucks come to take you in an unknown direction?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what was said, but it only lasted three hours and during the three hours no one came into the courtyard, and then the order was given for the men to return to the village again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The same man issued that same order? Dragan Micunovic?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The same order.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is the relationship between Gjon Prelaj and Dragan Micunovic? Why is he sending messages through this 15 year old boy?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gjon Prelaj lives near the house of Dragan and because there was no one older around, he was only 15 years old, he was maybe less than that, and there was no one else there, so he had to -- so he -- so Gjon was the one who was sent to tell the men, because there was no one older around. And my son, Blerim, is -- 15, was forced to go up into the hills too with his father.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, in all the versions, that is to say so paragraph that comes right after that, you refer to Milutin Prascevic. How is it that you know Milutin Prascevic?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him because he came into our courtyard and ordered us to leave the house within three hours. He told us not only us but everyone in the village, he first went to the family Dedaj and then to my house.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please describe this man to us, this man who entered your courtyard, this man by the name of Milutin Prascevic?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember he was big, corpulent, black hair. I don't know what else to say. I know that he came into our courtyard that day but I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How is it that you know his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked him. I asked him, "What is your name?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So he is issuing an order for you to leave your house, he's expelling you from your house, and you are asking him, "What's your name?"

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour that assumes facts in evidence. We haven't had evidence about what order things were said in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed. But it doesn't prevent the question being asked that way, for what value it has, Mr. Hannis. I don't think it's objectionable.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In line with my friend's objection, I'm going to rephrase my question. You tell us how the entire incident evolved.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean about Milutin Prascevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Describe that moment when he entered your courtyard. What happened? Also your conversation with him.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Easter Monday, on the 4th of April. First he went to the Dedaj family, and then he came back to my courtyard and my husband -- and ordered my husband to go away. And he said, "Better go voluntarily than under violence." I was near my husband at the time and I asked him, "What is your name?" I just asked him quite colloquially, and he told me that he was called Milutin Prascevic, and on that day, he didn't threaten us, there was no threat. We took our stuff with us, he gave us three hours, three hours. I got the children dressed and get everyone ready and we got on to the tractor and got on to the main road for Gjakova, me and all the rest of the village, within three hours. There was a whole line of people. They told us we could take the tractors but we would have to leave the cars in where they were. That's what we discussed with him. That's what I heard myself, with my own ears. And he spoke Albanian very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what happened then, after you left?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we left, we got to Sufadol. In Sufadol, Micunovic was there. I think his name was Aca, Aca he was called. He returned, as he turned us back, he told us to go back and all the people in the village believed him and we all returned to our houses. But during that time, nothing happened. We returned to our village and stayed there until the 27th of April and nothing happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One of the policemen told you to leave your house and another policeman was returning you to your homes. How much time elapsed between those two events?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: What could -- could you say that again, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Prascevic is forcing you out of your home. Micunovic is returning you to your homes. How much time elapsed between the two?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the first to the second, well, we were given three hours to get ourselves ready, and we got all our things together, and we were at the electric power station near the electric pole for an hour and it's not -- wasn't difficult going there on the tractor, and it might have been a bit more time, I don't remember, but I remember that he returned us. He sent us back. I remember that really well because I saw him and the men were talking to him and he told us to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, may I just end by putting one more question? I'm asking you how much time elapsed between your departure and your return, and that will be the end of my questions for before the break.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four to five hours altogether, going there and returning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does that include the three hours to get ready to go, or is that -- that includes the three hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. That includes the three hours we had to get ready and then the time going there and coming back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will break now and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Malaj --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Please carry on, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, before the break we were discussing the incident when Mr. Prascevic spoke to you. Where was he then, in your courtyard or inside your house?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was he with?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was inside the courtyard, when he was -- he was on his own, but on the road outside the courtyard there were others. But as I said, in the courtyard it was only him.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he speak in Albanian only with you?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: He spoke Albanian with everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You didn't know him from before?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you could only have known him by the name of Prascevic because you were told that by that particular person?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told us his name and his surname.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did he have a mustache or a beard and what was his approximate height? Could you describe him in brief? How old was he?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't measure him or I didn't ask about his age.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As regards beard or mustache, you didn't have to ask him that. Did he have any facial hair? How long was his hair?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: You told me earlier that he is tall -- you asked me, you asked me earlier whether he was tall, and soon after -- soon after we got orders from him to leave our own home, then my eyesight blurred because of that and I couldn't see anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, you cannot recall at all what he looked like?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot remember his appearance now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You gave a description of him earlier. You remember giving us some description?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Earlier I said he was tall, strongly built, but as for his face or anything, I can't -- I can't describe that. I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, did you see the policemen who were standing outside your courtyard?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we went out on the road, yes, I saw them, but not from very close.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From your courtyard, it was impossible for you to see them because there is a high wall around the house; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's correct. I couldn't see them from inside the courtyard but when we went out on to the road, yes, we saw them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the policemen who were outside of your courtyard?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you stop to talk with any of the policemen?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. What would I talk to them about? With the exception of Milutin inside the courtyard, I didn't talk to anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How much time did it take you to pass them by, since that was the only occasion you could establish any contact with them when you were leaving the house?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: What time are you talking about? Are you talking about how long Milutin stayed in the courtyard? He stayed for about ten minutes. And as for the rest, we were given three hours to get ready and then I told you earlier that it was about five hours altogether, leaving the place and coming back again, and we didn't kind of talk to them because they were not staying very close to us, and nobody was close to me, couldn't get any close to any of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, it took you only for a moment to pass by the policemen who were outside your courtyard as you were leaving your house?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: We convened where we convened, at the electric junction box. There were other people from the Dedaj family and there we saw the others, and Milutin was with my husband, and when we went to the gathering place, I did see them, but then we left and we didn't see them any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many other policemen were there in front of your house?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: In front of my house?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Were there any policemen in front of your house as you were leaving the house?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only one was Milutin. He was in the courtyard for ten, five, ten minutes, and the others were out on to the asphalted road. But inside my house, in the courtyard, it was only Milutin. The rest were out on the asphalted road.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: How many were there? These policemen on the asphalt road?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how many times I should say this. I said it was seven people on that road, seven policemen. All of them were heavily armed with machine-guns and knives and munitions, the way you armed your forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Milutin Prascevic was killed in Meja on the 21st of April 1999 at 1725?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: For this, I haven't heard. Up until after the 27th.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In that same incident, Boban Lazavic [phoen] was killed as well. Did you know that? He was a policeman and Lukdrag Lazarevic [phoen] was also killed, another policeman, as well as Naser Arifaj, who was an Albanian, a member of local security, then Miladin Domcic, a policeman. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. After the 27th, when we arrived in Albania and then after that, I learned about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you learn who killed them?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since you stated there were no KLA members there, did you assume, then, that they were killed by the Meja villagers?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm not sure she stated there were no KLA members there and I'm not sure where "there" is and when.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the basis for that proposition, Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness asserted that in that area, there were no KLA members, and that no one from her family and the villages around there was a member of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's not the note I have. My note is that that assertion was confined to her own village. If you can show me the transcript where I've got that wrong, then we can revise the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is difficult for me to refer back to the transcript. Perhaps it is easier for me to clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know, were there any KLA members in Meja?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There had never been but I -- as far as I'm aware, there weren't any KLA members there, but I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then I have to go back to my original question. Who, in your view, killed the four Serb policemen and one Albanian who was a member of a local security?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This witness is not here to give evidence of opinion. If she has knowledge of who was responsible, then you can ask her that. But you have to establish what knowledge she has, first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I would indicate that on page 34, line 4, she already said, "I don't know. I wasn't there," in response to the question about, Did you learn who killed them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There you have it, Mr. Lukic. It appears to have been answered already.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. That's why I tried to have the witness state her opinion, since she said she wasn't there but in any case I will move to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Since we were discussing Naser Arifaj, who was a member of the local security and who was killed, I wanted to ask you whether, in your village, there was such a thing as some sort of local security comprised of Albanians.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether in any of the villages nearby there was a local security comprised of Albanians?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. At the time we were in our homes, we didn't have information about other places. I can tell you everything about what happened in my house but I don't know other things that happened in other places. I don't know why you're asking me about these things.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I am not sure whether we understand each other. When I say a local security or a local security force, I have in mind locals, Albanians, armed by the state and people who hail from that area, from that village in which they carried out their tasks, their tasks being establishing law and order instead of the police. Was there such a force or formation in your village?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There wasn't anything like that in our village.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. To go to your statement dated the 6th of September 2001, I have a paragraph reference for the B/C/S and the English, but I need to establish the same for the Albanian version as well, if I may have one moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I think if you just carry on, Mr. Hannis will be able to give you the Albanian paragraph number.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the B/C/S this is page 2, the fifth and the sixth paragraphs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And in the English?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that would be [Microphone not activated]. In the English I assume that's five and six as well. On her copy of the Albanian I believe it would be beginning with the last half of paragraph 4 and paragraph 5 on to paragraph 6 on the following page.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first of the two paragraphs, Mrs. Malaj, you talk about Prascevic's arrival to your house and when he told you to go, to leave. In the first paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour, I think I've misdirected her then because I thought we were talking about her statement from the 6th of September 2001.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's what he said but it's not on the second page. It's the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see it's in the middle of the fourth paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's in the fourth paragraph in the English on page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Then I have directed her to the correct place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Please carry on, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There you state that Prascevic came to your house and told you to leave. You said, "We got ready right away and we took some things with us." You climbed on the tractor, or rather into the trailer, and you set out.

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, you state, "We all gathered at 6.30 a.m. And formed a convoy." Did you leave in the evening or in the morning?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: My English says p.m., Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So does mine. The English copies say p.m.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Sorry, I follow the B/C/S version and it says in the morning. So we'll skip. I withdraw this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To move on to page 3 of the English, paragraph 1, and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, paragraph 1 in the B/C/S, paragraph 2 in the English, and in the Albanian version, paragraph 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here, you yourself noticed some discrepancies in your statements. Here you state you reached the village of Sufadol, instead of the village of Meja when you were returned home by Aco Micunovic. How far did you get before you were told to turn back?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got up to Sufadol, and that's where we were turned back. They didn't let us go any farther, to -- on that day. Q.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Before you go on, what's the distance between Meja and Sufadol? Could you please answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Meja is a bit farther away than Sufadol. Sufadol is the first village after Korenica, where it's quite near, quite near, and Meja is farther away from us. It's on the other side, on the other side of our village, on the other side of the road, I mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're saying that you were not allowed to continue, that they didn't allow you to do that. In other words, you wanted to continue on your journey; however, the police would not allow to you do that and they told you to go back home; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the way it was. We were acting under their orders and did what they said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like to ask you to ponder on the moment when you left Kosovo to go towards Albania. Where did you leave Kosovo and where did you enter Albania?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: We left Kosova on the 27th of April at 7 in the morning. It was a terrible day for us. We were forced to leave Kosova. We went to Prizren by foot. They didn't even give us any water or food or clothing, nothing. Only God helped us. And it was only by God's help that we arrived at the border alive. The whole day, the whole night, until the next day, until 1.00, we got to the border and got over the border.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, the question was a specific question. Where was it that you crossed the border? That was the question. Are you able to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh, sorry. I was thinking about the time. I don't remember what the place was called. It was the last village. I can read it. I can find it here in the statement because I've forgotten the name. It's called Qafa e Morines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that this was a very stressful event for you and you remember it very well, don't you?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an absolutely terrible thing, and I will never forget it as long as I live.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could we now have the map of the municipality of Djakovica? This is Exhibit P35. As a matter of fact, we won't need this map because it does not depict everything that we want to show the Trial Chamber. Could we please see the map of entire Kosovo, or at least its southern part?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] I'm trying to figure it out, Your Honour. Just give me one second. [Interpretation] Could anybody amongst my colleagues help me? Does anybody know the exhibit number of the map of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, there are many maps of Kosovo circulating. ;. Mr. Hannis can you assist?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour I'm not sure what he wants to show. One map that we have shown this witness that shows Korenica, Djakovica, Prizren and the border crossing point, is P23.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] That will do. That will be excellent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can we start making some progress, please? The production is there on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: P44, please, if it could be shown. Obviously we'll have to continue without the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that P44?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. It's not visible on this map what I want to show.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour the Kosovo atlas is Exhibit P16 which has several maps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We need to know the page, though, and counsel doesn't seem to be prepared for this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Malaj, in your first statement, on page 4 of the B/C/S version, paragraph 3, which is the fourth page of the English version, paragraph 3, and the fifth page, paragraph 2, of the Albanian version, you stated, "We arrived at the border crossing Kukes on the following day at 1300 hours. That border crossing is in Prizren municipality." In your second statement page 4, paragraph 6 of the B/C/S, page 5, paragraph 2 of the English version, and page 5, the last paragraph of the Albanian version, as well as the first paragraph on the sixth page thereof, you say, "We arrived at the Qafa e Morines border crossing with Albania at noon on the 28th of April 1999." These two border crossings are some 30 to 40 kilometres apart, Madam. Did you tell the truth to the investigators of the ICTY when you gave your first statement to them?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to that form of the question. I think if we look at our map, that you will see that there is not a good basis for this question. Mr. Bakrac went through the same thing with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is not an appropriate way at the moment to go about this exercise although I don't see anything wrong with exploring the issue itself. But can I ask first of all, Mrs. Malaj, this question: It would appear that border crossings have names. Were you personally aware of the name of the point at which you crossed the border?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was called Qafa e Morines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And you personally knew that? That was information you knew? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And how long did it take you to get from there to Kukes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From Qafa e Morines crossing, we were about -- it was about one hour it took to cross the border, and then up to Kukes, we spent a couple of hours at the border itself, three hours, and then we got trucks, into trucks, and were driven to Kukes, and in Kukes we were two or three days and then we were sent on to Durres and then Tirana.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can you remember how long the journey in the truck from the border or from where you were near the border to Kukes took?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it took several hours. I don't really remember but I would think over eight hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's from Qafa e Morines to Kukes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you travel in the direction of Prizren from your place, from your house?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the direction we took.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And this is south from Korenica, is it not? Or in the direction of southeast?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: From our village, we went to Prizren. I thought it was in a westerly direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [In English] Now we'll try to show the map. It's Kosovo atlas map number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the exhibit number of the Kosovo atlas?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have the ERN number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe that's P615, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: 615, it now appears to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's very hard to follow this and that's the not the map I need. We have one map and if it could be put on the ELMO it would be much easier and we would be able to see what we want to show.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Which map is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have a Kosovo map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is one that's not already an exhibit?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I don't know how to solve it differently because we need border crossings with the names and on these maps we couldn't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Let's put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just want to state my objection that this sort of violates the order about us getting documents they are going to be used in cross-examination ahead of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's a map, it's not a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: A map is a document, Mr. Lukic. Please, the order applies to anything that's going to be exhibited. But I have not formed the impression that this was being deliberately withheld. I think it's being tendered as a potential solution to a difficulty that wasn't anticipated and therefore, for that reason I think it ought to be put on the ELMO. So that's how we'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Please go down. We want to see Djakovica. Can you go down, please? We want to see Djakovica and Prizren. Yes. Further on. Further on. We see Prizren. Now go, we want to see left part of the -- bit more, bit more, and then again down. Now we see it. Down, go down. [Microphone not activated] Okay. Stop there. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mrs. Malaj, in your left upper corner there, left of Djakovica, northwest from Korenica, can you see a name underlined in yellow, the Chamber is Qafa e Morines?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to pose an interjection at this point. This map appears to be in Serbian rather than in Albanian. That may explain the difference that I anticipate is coming up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may do but let's hear the questions and answers first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On the west side and left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see Prizren there? Did you go from the direction of Djakovica in the direction of Prizren?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Gjakova to Prizren, and then from Prizren we went towards the border. And Qafa e Morines, I don't know what it's called in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You said that you went towards Kukes and on the map, it says Vrbnica?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This will be left from Prizren. Southwest from Prizren, that is. What you are showing now is Macedonia. It reads Kukci [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not going to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is where you crossed?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That, you can see Kukci?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
utterances.text: We went from Prizren, yeah, here but we call it differently. We have a different word. It's called but it's called that way too. But that was where we were, and from about 12 to 1.00 until we got across the border, and then that's at that place they took our documents away but they couldn't take them because we didn't have them. They call it Vrbnica, eh? We call it Qafa e Morines. There is Qafa Pruset [phoen], that's the other crossing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And above Pruset, when you go further up, you will see that it says Qafa e Morines?

utterances.speaker: Lizane Malaj [Resumed]
